subtitles.plaintext:
iadls instrumental activities of daily living 
these are key life skills that we usually
learn as teenagers and that are necessary to live 
independently as adults they require more complex
thinking skills and often require organizational 
skills they include things like managing finances
such as paying bills and managing financial assets 
managing transportation either via driving or by
organizing some other means of transport shopping 
and meal preparation this covers everything
required to get a meal on the table it also covers 
shopping for clothes or other items required for
daily life house cleaning and home maintenance 
this means cleaning kitchens after eating
keeping one's living space reasonably clean 
and tidy and keeping up with home maintenance
managing communication such as with telephone 
and mail and nowadays also managing email and the
computer there's managing medications which covers 
obtaining medications and taking them as directed
you

subtitles.plaintext:
Let's start with activities of daily living or ADL's.
ADL's are foundational self-care skills that we usually learn as very
young children.
They're also sometimes called basic ADL's or BADL's.
They include walking,
or otherwise getting around the home or outside,
also feeding,
as in being able to get food from a plate into
one's mouth,
dressing, as in selecting appropriate clothes for the weather and the
occasion and being able to put them on,
then there's grooming,
which means adequately managing your personal appearance,
such as managing your hair,
doing your makeup or shaving.
Next toileting,
which means getting to and from the toilet,
using it appropriately,
and cleaning oneself.
And then there's bathing,
which means washing one's face and body in the bath or
shower.

if you're not exercising what's most

um small is often a safer way to to

people start seeing benefits within you

you really want the benefit then you
want to think about how to make sure you
fit in these four types of exercise and
that is um strength uh exercise also

also known as endurance or cardio
balance exercises and flexibility
exercises

subtitles.plaintext:
as a geriatric medical doctor one of the top 
questions I get from families is this how do
I get my aging parent with memory loss to accept 
or understand that they need help so here's the
truth based on my years of experience as 
a geriatrician in the early stages of this
memory loss Journey many older adults won't be 
able to accept or understand that they need help
so if you want to be able to help your parent you 
actually need to do what we do as geriatricians
stop the explanations and stop focusing on getting 
them to accept or understand and when you do this
two things will happen first you'll have fewer 
arguments with them and next you'll be freed up to
practice a better way of speaking to them in which 
you work with and around their reality instead of
fighting to change their reality if you'd like to 
learn this better way of speaking to your parent
with memory loss check out my free online training 
in which I'll teach you a step-by-step method
that you can put to use right away take care and 
thanks for all you're doing to help your parent
